terce (prayer at the third hour of daylight)
tierce (a stance with the back of the hand facing up and the knuckles outwards)
An attack from such a position.
Terz.et:
Inherited from Middle High German tërzje, tërze, from Latin tertia. Doublet of Tertia.
The musical sense was a later semantic loan from Italian terza.

s: stink, fight, trouble (aggressive, quarrelsome behavior; typically as part of protesting or looking for a fight)
to raise a stink, to make a scene
Jung möchte er nicht mehr sein, weil die Katastrophen erst noch bevorstehen. Wenn er aber jung wäre, dann würde er ein Revoluzzer sein wollen, „Terz machen“.
He doesn't want to be young anymore, because the disasters are still to come. But if he were to be young, he would want to be a revolutionary, raise a stink.
fuss (seemingly disproportionate occurence of effort or issues to achieve a goal)
Wir numerieren die Tage ab sofort einfach durch! Das spart auch Platz, zumindest die nächste Zeit - und wir schenken uns den ganzen Terz mit den ewigen Geburtstagen, Jahrestagen, Weihnachten etc.!!
We'll just give every day a running number from now on! It saves space, at least in the short term - and we don't need to bother with all the fuss about birthdays, anniversaries, christmas, etc.!!
Ich bin für jede Hilfe dankbar, wollte aber eigentlich nicht so einen Terz mit extra Becken und später Aufzuchtsschalen und so machen.
I'm grateful for any help, but to be honest I didn't want to do all that fuss with a separate tank and breeding bowls and so on later on.
Terz.et: Küpper derives it from a regional sense of "strike" of Terz f (etymology 1), likely originating in the fencing sense, contaminated with regional Dez m (“head”), originally in North-Western Germany. He dates it to the 1960s.

Termite.et: From the Late Latin termes, late variant of the Classical Latin tarmes (“woodworm”).

s: Aber die royalistischen Terroristen, die Terroristen von Gottes- und Rechts-Gnaden, in der Praxis sind sie brutal, verächtlich, gemein, in der Theorie feig, versteckt, doppelzüngig, in beiden Bezienungen ehrlos.
But the royal terrorists, the terrorists by the grace of God and the law, are in practice brutal, disdainful and mean, in theory cowardly, secretive and deceitful, and in both respects disreputable.
Wir sind rücksichtslos, wir verlangen keine Rücksicht von euch. Wenn die Reihe an uns kömmt, wir werden den Terrorismus nicht beschönigen.
We are compassionless and we ask no compassion from you. When our turn comes, we shall not make excuses for the terrorism.

Terpentin.et: From Middle Dutch terpentijn, from Old French terbentine, turbentine, Latin terebinthīna, from terebintha, from Ancient Greek τερεβινθίνη (terebinthínē), from τερεβινθινος (terebinthinos), from τερέβινθος (terébinthos). See also turpentine.

tertiär.et: From French tertiaire, from Medieval Latin tertiarius.

terrisch.et: From Middle High German tœrisch (“foolish, daft”), from Middle High German tôr, tôre (“fool”). Synchronically analysable as Tor (“fool”) + -isch.

a municipality of Lower Austria, Austria
the fourth and fifth class of Gymnasium
Terek sandpiper (bird of the species Xenus cinereus)

Terzel.et: From Middle French terçuel, from Late Latin tertiolus, a diminutive of Latin tertius (“third”). Semantics unclear.

Terpen.et: Derived from Terpentin. Coined by German chemist August Kekulé in 1866.

s: a surname of Westphalian and Lower Rhenish origin
Terlinden.et: From Middle Low German ter linden (“by the linden tree”).

s: a Westphalian surname, notably held by Josef Terboven (governor of German-occupied Norway)
Terboven.et: From Middle Low German dâr bōven (literally “up there”), referring to a farmstead on a hill above a village. The first syllable was altered through contraction and subsequent adaptation to Low German ter (“to the”) as in names like Terlinden. Compare the varia…

s: a male given name from Latin, equivalent to English Terence
Ich gebe dir einen Hofstaat / Von steifgeputzten Sonetten, / Stolzen Terzinen und höflichen Stanzen;

Terrier.et: Ultimately from Middle French, from Old French chien terrier (“terrier dog”), from chien (“dog”) + Old French terrier (“of earth”, adjective), from Medieval Latin terrarius (“of earth”), from Latin terra (“earth”).

s: tertiarization (the process of transition to a service-based economy)
Die Tertiärisierung hat in den letzten Jahrzehnten dazu geführt, dass über 70 Prozent der Erwerbstätigen im Dienstleistungssektor arbeiten.
Tertiarization has led to over 70 percent of employees working in the service sector in recent decades.
Tertiärisierung.et: Derived from Latin tertiarius (“concerning the third part”), from tertius (“third”), + suffix -ierung.

s: tertiary sector (the segment of the economy that provides services to consumers and other businesses)
In hochentwickelten Volkswirtschaften entfallen über 70 Prozent der Bruttowertschöpfung auf den Tertiärsektor.
In highly developed economies, over 70 percent of gross value added comes from the tertiary sector.
futures market, derivatives market (a financial market where participants buy and sell commodity and futures contracts for delivery on a specified future date)
Unternehmen nutzen den Terminmarkt, um sich gegen Preisschwankungen in der Industriegesellschaft abzusichern und Planungssicherheit für ihre Wirtschaftskraft zu gewinnen.
Companies use the futures market to hedge against price fluctuations in industrial society and to gain planning security for their economic power.
Im modernen Wissenssektor ermöglicht der Terminmarkt eine präzise Steuerung der Zahlungskraft, indem zukünftige Cashflows bereits heute fixiert werden.
In the modern knowledge sector, the derivatives market enables precise management of solvency by fixing future cash flows today.
